title: Basic Question
description: Fundamental question defining Agentic AI

inputConversation.content: What is Agentic AI?

expectedBehavior: Defines agentic AI as autonomous systems capable of planning, goal pursuit, and tool usage.

title: Immediate Follow-Up
description: Follow-up question without restating the subject

inputConversation.content: What is Agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to autonomous systems capable of taking actions to achieve specified goals.
What are its applications?

expectedBehavior: Answers with agentic AI applications (software development, research, customer operations) resolving 'its' to Agentic AI.

title: Pronoun Resolution
description: Resolving 'it' to the subject of the previous turns

inputConversation.content: Tell me about Agentic AI.
Agentic AI is an autonomous computing paradigm.
Which companies are developing it?

expectedBehavior: Resolves 'it' to Agentic AI and names relevant companies (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Microsoft).

title: Contextual Comparison
description: Comparing the first two entities listed in prior assistant turn

inputConversation.content: Name three top vector databases.
Three top vector databases are: 1. Pinecone, 2. Qdrant, and 3. Milvus.
Compare the first two.

expectedBehavior: Compares Pinecone (managed SaaS) and Qdrant (open-source Rust engine) specifically.

title: Contextual Reference (The Second One)
description: Selecting the second item from an enumerated list

inputConversation.content: What are the key components of an LLM agent?
The key components are: 1. Planning, 2. Memory, and 3. Tools.
Tell me more about the second one.

expectedBehavior: Explains Memory (short-term, working, and persistent long-term storage) without confusion.

title: Topic Transition
description: Abrupt shift to a completely different technical domain

inputConversation.content: Tell me about Agentic AI.
Agentic AI focuses on autonomous goal pursuit.
Now explain PostgreSQL.

expectedBehavior: Explains PostgreSQL (relational database, ACID, SQL) without bleeding previous AI agent definitions.

title: Return to Previous Topic
description: Returning to a prior subject after an intermediate diversion

inputConversation.content: What is Agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to autonomous goal-directed systems.
Now explain PostgreSQL.
PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database system.
Coming back to Agentic AI, what are its limitations?

expectedBehavior: Discusses limitations of Agentic AI (hallucinations, infinite loops, high cost, predictability) rather than PostgreSQL limitations.

title: Multi-Turn Reasoning
description: Step-by-step query refinement, comparison, and final synthesis

inputConversation.content: What is Fastify?
Fastify is a fast and low-overhead web framework for Node.js.
How does it compare to Express in throughput?
Fastify offers substantially higher throughput than Express due to its custom router and fast-json-stringify schema serialization.
Summarize the architectural reasons for that difference.

expectedBehavior: Synthesizes the architectural reasons (radix tree routing, pre-compiled JSON schemas, minimal prototype pollution).

title: Ambiguous Reference Handling
description: User provides an unresolved demonstrative pronoun

inputConversation.content: What about that one?

expectedBehavior: Asks ONE short clarifying question instead of hallucinating a topic, adhering to Core Directive 7.

title: Missing Context / Unmentioned Topic
description: User asks about an entity never mentioned in conversation

inputConversation.content: Why did we decide against using Redis?

expectedBehavior: States that Redis was not previously discussed in this conversation.

title: Long Conversation Context Retention
description: Maintains key project constraints after 8 conversational turns

inputConversation.content: My primary database constraint is zero vector databases.
Understood. No vector databases will be used.
Tell me about TypeScript strict mode.
Strict mode enables all strict type checking options.
What port should Fastify run on?
Fastify typically runs on port 3000 or 3001.
What was my initial database constraint?

expectedBehavior: Accurately recalls the zero vector databases constraint.

title: Repeated Question Consistency
description: Asking identical query twice yields logically consistent facts

inputConversation.content: What does ACID stand for?
ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.
What does ACID stand for?

expectedBehavior: Provides the identical, correct expansion of ACID.

title: Conversation Switching Isolation
description: Switches to an isolated conversation without cross-talk leakage

inputConversation.content: What is the capital of Italy?

expectedBehavior: Answers Rome without any leakage from previous conversation threads.

title: Follow-Up After Reload State
description: Continuing from an active loaded conversation

inputConversation.content: I am designing a cache with TTL.
A TTL cache expires entries after a set duration.
What eviction policy should I pair with it?

expectedBehavior: Recommends LRU (Least Recently Used) or LFU in the context of the TTL cache.

title: Summary Request
description: User requests a concise summary of the entire session

inputConversation.content: We are building Recall AI using React, Fastify, and PostgreSQL.
Got it. That is a solid full-stack TypeScript stack.
Summarize what we discussed.

expectedBehavior: Summarizes Recall AI, React, Fastify, and PostgreSQL.

title: Reference Resolution Across Multiple Turns
description: Referencing an entity introduced 4 turns ago

inputConversation.content: Let's track a product named ChronoDesk.
Tracking ChronoDesk.
What are its main competitors?
Competitors include Linear, Asana, and Jira.
How does ChronoDesk differentiate itself?

expectedBehavior: Synthesizes differentiation for ChronoDesk relative to Linear, Asana, and Jira.

title: Context Retention After Rapid Topic Changes
description: Recovers subject after interleaved topic changes

inputConversation.content: Plan an architecture for Recall AI.
We will use Fastify with SSE and PostgreSQL.
Quick question: what is 15 * 12?
Back to the architecture, how does the frontend stream messages?

expectedBehavior: Explains SSE (Server-Sent Events) streaming with fetchEventSource or EventSource.

title: Multiple Entities with Similar Names
description: Differentiating between Next.js, Nuxt.js, and NestJS

inputConversation.content: I am confused between Next.js, Nuxt.js, and NestJS.
Next.js is for React, Nuxt.js is for Vue, and NestJS is a Node.js backend framework.
Which one is for Vue?

expectedBehavior: Identifies Nuxt.js specifically without confusing it with Next.js or NestJS.

title: Follow-Up Using Incomplete Sentences
description: Elliptical user question: 'And PostgreSQL?'

inputConversation.content: Does SQLite support concurrency?
SQLite supports one writer at a time, limiting high concurrency.
And PostgreSQL?

expectedBehavior: Understands the elliptical question as asking about PostgreSQL's concurrency (MVCC, multiple simultaneous writers and readers).

title: Contradictory User-Provided Context
description: User asserts an untrue premise: 'Since Python is statically typed...'

inputConversation.content: Since Python is statically typed, why do we need type hints?

expectedBehavior: Politely corrects the contradiction, explaining that Python is dynamically typed.
